answer.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing is the loudest signal, but memory_73 explicitly records that promotional pricing bought acquisition at the cost of 30-day retention and warns against generalizing it — that directly conflicts with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so I decline the price match. The two internal declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are the tractable levers, and both memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer signup fields lifts first-week activation) point at the same funnel stage. Onboarding is the upstream cause: fixing completion should propagate into activation, whereas activation_messaging (memory_91) treats the symptom further downstream. I verify memory_86 and memory_31 because they are the two I am actually betting on and both are the oldest/most-likely-stale records being applied to a changed competitive environment — I want the original records to confirm the lift was durable rather than a novelty effect, and to check whether the cohorts resemble today's SMB mix. Risk flagged: cutting signup fields or onboarding steps can degrade lead qualification and downstream data quality, so 'activation' can rise while qualified revenue does not; I will instrument qualified-pipeline and 30-day retention, not just completion rate. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout, since the inherited lifts were measured in a pre-competitor environment and may not transfer cleanly.
